B05_00: SLIT-ROBO signalling lets a growing axon cross a source of repellent cue exactly once. Beforehand, Netrin-1 acting on DCC attracts the axon while ROBO3 dampens the repulsive receptors ROBO1 and ROBO2 so SLIT is ignored, with NELL2 read through ROBO3 adding steering. Afterwards, SLIT-bound ROBO binds DCC and silences netrin attraction, ROBO3 is downregulated, and SRC-family kinases drive cytoskeletal remodelling that expels the axon.
B05_01: Sema4D binding to plexin-B1 reshapes the actin cytoskeleton, driving cell migration or growth cone collapse depending on context. The plexin-B1 tail recruits the RhoA exchange factors ARHGEF11 and ARHGEF12 and binds RND1, and ERBB2 association couples it to RhoA, RhoB and RhoC. ROCK1 and ROCK2 then phosphorylate myosin light chains and activate LIM kinases, so myosin II contractility builds stress fibres and focal adhesions or collapses peripheral actin.
B05_02: The scaffold AKAP5 binds the guidance receptors ROBO2 and ROBO3.1 and brings protein kinase A, protein kinase C and the calcium-dependent phosphatase calcineurin next to them. Guidance signalling is thereby read out alongside cAMP and calcium cues, and recruited PKC phosphorylates ROBO3.1. Such anchoring confines broadly acting kinases to membrane microdomains, linking receptor engagement to cytoskeletal remodelling.
B05_03: CHL1 is an immunoglobulin-superfamily adhesion receptor that does not bind itself, so its signalling depends on partners: contactin-6 in trans, beta1 integrins engaged through RGD and DGEA motifs, and neuropilin-1, through which it converts Semaphorin-3A into growth cone collapse. Its cytoplasmic tail binds ankyrin, linking adhesion to the spectrin cytoskeleton and translating guidance cues into cytoskeletal change for neurite extension and axon steering.
B05_04: Growth cones advance by gripping the substrate at the front and releasing it at the back, an asymmetry maintained by recycling the adhesion molecule L1. ERM proteins couple ligand-bound L1 to retrograde actin flow, generating traction. AP-2 reads a tyrosine motif in the L1 tail only when unphosphorylated, so SRC phosphorylation retains L1 peripherally while dephosphorylation licenses clathrin-dependent endocytosis; kinesins and shootin-1 return internalised L1 forward.
B05_05: Netrin-1 becomes a repulsive steering signal for axons displaying UNC5 receptors. Netrin binding to UNC5A-D promotes phosphorylation within the receptor ZU-5 domain, and Src-family kinases with the phosphatase SHP2 relay the signal to the growth cone actin cytoskeleton. Long-range repulsion needs DCC, whose cytoplasmic domain pairs with UNC5, whereas UNC5 alone suffices at short range; unoccupied UNC5 also triggers cell death as a dependence receptor.
B05_06: DSCAM and DSCAML1 are immunoglobulin-superfamily adhesion receptors whose homophilic cell-to-cell binding mediates self-recognition and the repulsion that keeps sister branches and like cells from overlapping, setting neurite and cell body spacing. DSCAM also cooperates with the netrin receptor DCC in responding to netrin-1, linking adhesive contact to attractive axon turning. Overall, cell-surface adhesion feeds into axon pathfinding, layer targeting and the wiring precision of circuits.
B05_07: NrCAM is an L1-family adhesion receptor bridging guidance signalling and cytoskeletal organisation through three kinds of contact. A cytoplasmic ankyrin-binding segment couples it to the spectrin cytoskeleton, clustering receptors at specialised axonal membrane domains. A C-terminal PDZ-binding motif engages SAP97/SAP102/PSD-95 scaffolds, linking it into submembrane protein networks, while extracellularly it binds contactin TAG-1 to promote neurite outgrowth and partners neuropilin-2 to convert class 3 semaphorins into repulsive axon turning.
B05_08: Ankyrins anchor L1 family adhesion molecules to the membrane skeleton, positioning adhesion and excitability machinery on the cell surface. Ankyrin-G, -B and -R bind the tails of L1CAM, neurofascin and NrCAM and tether them, with sodium and KCNQ2/KCNQ3 potassium channels, to spectrin-actin networks. This restrains lateral diffusion, strengthens homophilic adhesion, and concentrates sodium channels at axon initial segments and nodes for action potential initiation and propagation.
B05_09: Beyond the canonical class 3 semaphorin to plexin-A route, transmembrane and GPI-anchored semaphorins engage plexins of the A, B, C and D subfamilies and non-plexin partners to steer repulsion, fasciculation and cell behaviour. Specificity comes from receptor combinations: SEMA4D acting through CD72, SEMA4A and SEMA6 members engaging plexin-A, SEMA7A signalling through integrin alpha1/beta1, SEMA6D working with the TREM2-TYROBP adaptor pair, and SEMA3E-PLXND1 restricting sprouting.
B05_10: This branch of SLIT-ROBO signalling reshapes actin by raising RHOA activity. SLIT2-bound ROBO1 engages the unconventional myosin MYO9B and blocks its RHOA GTPase-activating function, so GTP-bound RHOA accumulates. ROCK then phosphorylates myosin regulatory light chain, generating actomyosin contractility that steers axons and limits cell migration, showing how a receptor can activate a GTPase by inhibiting an inhibitor rather than recruiting an exchange factor.
B05_11: Neurofascin is an L1-family adhesion molecule whose isoforms organise specialised axonal membrane domains needed for saltatory conduction. The 186 kDa form clusters at nodes with NrCAM, anchored to the spectrin cytoskeleton through ankyrin, while the 155 kDa form works with contactin and CNTNAP1 to build paranodal axo-glial junctions. A C-terminal PDZ-binding motif recruits syntenin-1, linking adhesion to intracellular scaffolding and trafficking.
B05_12: Dendritic branching reuses a guidance cue system that normally repels axons. SLIT1 binds the receptors ROBO1 and ROBO2 on dendrites and, instead of causing retraction, promotes formation of new branch points, setting how many synaptic inputs a cell can receive. The adaptor NCK2 couples activated ROBO to actin regulatory machinery and is required for branching, showing that a cue's interpretation depends on which effector is engaged where.
B05_13: Netrin-1 binding to DCC steers growing axons, and whether a growth cone turns toward or away depends on the second messengers it generates. DCC engages phospholipase C gamma, aided by phosphatidylinositol transfer, to produce IP3 and diacylglycerol. IP3 releases calcium from ER stores, diacylglycerol directly gates TRPC3 and TRPC6, and store depletion recruits other TRPC channels; the resulting calcium influx, tuned by cyclic nucleotide levels, determines attraction versus repulsion.
B05_14: Ephrin-B ligands on a neighbouring cell activate EphB receptors, and this forward signalling turns cell contact into dendritic spine and synapse formation as motile filopodia find partners and mature into spines that recruit NMDA receptors. Clustered receptors engage Src-family kinases and FAK and recruit intersectin and kalirin to activate CDC42 and RAC1, driving Arp2/3 actin branching and PAK signalling, while RHOA-ROCK-LIMK phosphorylates cofilin.
B05_15: Sema3A binds neuropilin-1, which pairs with a plexin-A receptor to transduce a repulsive signal that switches off substrate adhesion, so a neurite or migrating cell loses traction and turns away. Plexin GAP activity toward R-Ras lowers integrin affinity for ligand, while Rnd1 and Rac1 gate plexin activation, FARP2 acts as an exchange factor, and Src-family and Fes kinases relay phosphorylation. Talin and PIP5K1C link the output to focal adhesion assembly.
B05_16: Semaphorin 4D acting through plexin-B1 converts a guidance cue into loss of integrin-mediated adhesion and collapse of the leading edge. Ligand binding lets Rnd1 engage plexin-B1 and switch on its GTPase-activating domain, lowering active R-Ras; reduced PI3K-Akt output relieves inhibition of GSK-3beta, which phosphorylates and inactivates the microtubule assembly factor CRMP2. Meanwhile p190RhoGAP transiently lowers RhoA-GTP and Rac1 is redirected, so actin and microtubule dynamics favour retraction over protrusion.
B05_17: The abundance of SLIT ligands and ROBO receptors, which determines responses to repellent cues, is set at every step from gene to protein. LIM-homeodomain factors and HOXA2 drive ROBO and SLIT transcription, and the RNA-binding protein MSI1 boosts ROBO3 translation. Ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation tune protein levels, opposed by the deubiquitinase USP33 stabilising ROBO1, while dystroglycan and collagen IV anchor secreted SLITs.
B05_18: When a B-type ephrin meets an EPH receptor on another cell, the ligand sends a reverse signal into its own cell, making contact signalling bidirectional. In one route, Src-family kinases such as FYN phosphorylate ephrin tail tyrosines, recruiting NCK2 and, through GIT1, ARHGEF7 and PAK, driving RAC1-dependent actin and myosin remodelling. Alternatively, a C-terminal PDZ-binding motif engages scaffolds such as syntenin, coupling adhesion to junctional organisation.
B05_19: RAC1 activation converts a repulsive SLIT cue into growth cone actin remodelling, acting as a set point rather than an on-off switch, since low RAC1 activity sustains outgrowth. SLIT2-bound ROBO1 exposes motifs that recruit the adaptors NCK1 or NCK2, which bring the exchange factors SOS1 and SOS2 to the membrane to load GTP onto RAC1. Active RAC1 engages PAK kinases, linking receptor occupancy to actin and adhesion dynamics.
B05_20: Sema3A makes growth cones collapse and turn away, and its PAK-dependent arm converts receptor binding into actin disassembly. Signal reception requires neuropilin-1 as the ligand-binding subunit with a plexin-A receptor. Rac1 recruited to the complex activates group I PAK kinases, which phosphorylate LIMK1; LIMK1 phosphorylates cofilin, blocking its actin-severing and depolymerising activity and remodelling filaments in the collapsing growth cone, with Src-family and Fes kinases and HSP90 supporting transmission.
B05_21: Contact between EPH receptor-bearing and ephrin-bearing cells usually ends in withdrawal. Because the trans EPH-ephrin interaction is high affinity, adhesion must be actively dismantled: ADAM10 and matrix metalloproteinases cleave ligand or receptor, gamma-secretase processes the remaining stub, and clathrin- and dynamin-dependent endocytosis internalises intact complexes. Src-family kinases transmit the signal, while RAC1 activated by TIAM1 and VAV drives actin remodelling that retracts the membrane.
B05_22: The adhesion molecule L1CAM acts as a receptor converting extracellular contact into decisions about axon growth, guidance and migration. Partnering with beta1 and beta3 integrins, L1 triggers Src-family kinases, VAV2, RAC1 and PAK1, then MEK1/2-ERK1/2 signalling that drives motility and outgrowth. L1 is also an obligate neuropilin-1 co-receptor for Sema3A-induced growth cone collapse, while homophilic binding mediates attraction; FGFR1 and casein kinase 2 add control.
B05_23: Collapsin response mediator proteins convert the repellent Sema3A into growth cone cytoskeletal change. Sema3A binds a neuropilin-1 and plexin-A receptor whose cytoplasmic tail holds CRMP1 and related DPYSL proteins near the kinases that modify them. Sequential phosphorylation by Fyn-recruited Cdk5 with p35, by Fes and by GSK3beta strips CRMPs of their tubulin-binding ability, so microtubule assembly stalls and F-actin depolymerises, collapsing the growth cone and turning the axon away.
B05_24: Ephrin-A binding to EPHA receptors makes growth cones collapse and retract, keeping axons out of ephrin-rich territory and ordering graded projections. Ligand engagement clusters receptors and recruits Src-family kinases, which phosphorylate the exchange factor ephexin (NGEF) and shift it toward RHOA activation while Cdc42 and Rac1 signalling falls. RHOA activates ROCK1 and ROCK2 to phosphorylate myosin light chains, and myosin II contraction outpaces actin extension, disassembling filopodia and lamellipodia.
B05_25: DCC converts a netrin-1 gradient into growth cone attraction. Lacking catalytic activity, DCC associates with FAK, Src and Fyn, which on netrin binding phosphorylate its tail and recruit adaptors such as NCK1 and DOCK1. These feed RAC1, CDC42 and the exchange factor TRIO, while WASL and ABLIM proteins remodel actin, producing asymmetric polymerisation and filopodial extension on the netrin-facing side.
B05_26: This branch of SLIT-ROBO signalling collapses actin-based protrusions at the growth cone leading edge by inactivating CDC42 and RAC1, steering axons away and positioning migrating cells. SLIT2-bound ROBO1 exposes a cytoplasmic motif that recruits the GAPs SRGAP1-3 and ARHGAP39, which stimulate GTP hydrolysis on CDC42 and RAC1, returning them to the inactive GDP-bound state. Reduced Rho GTPase activity withdraws filopodial and lamellipodial drive.
B05_27: ABL kinases convert the SLIT repellent signal received by ROBO receptors into cytoskeletal change. ABL1 and ABL2 phosphorylate effectors that reorganise the growth cone and also phosphorylate ROBO1 itself, tuning its sensitivity to further SLIT. Their partners span both cytoskeletal systems, CAP1 and CAP2 governing actin filament turnover and CLASP1 and CLASP2 acting on microtubule plus ends, coordinating filopodial collapse with microtubule behaviour.
